title: When the Semester Burns
premise: Mirabel Fairweather just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollowmere Academy, a school built atop a burned-out conservatory from a century ago. But when the school's legendary ghost, the Ash Girl, starts leaving notes in ink that appears only to him, he discovers she is the erased memory of a student the school wronged—and that his own family helped bury her story. As the notes pull him toward the winter arts showcase's final audition, Mirabel must choose between protecting his new friendships and the comfortable lie of his anonymity, or unsealing the truth and giving the Ash Girl her name back. In the end, he performs her unfinished piece at the audition, the school's records burn open, and Mirabel steps into the light under his own chosen name.
about_author: Astrid Thackeray is a former boarding-school music teacher who spent years cataloguing the archives of institutions that preferred their histories unexamined. She writes ghost-adjacent YA about quiet kids who learn that being seen is worth the burn.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Mirabel's POV. Mirabel maps Hollowmere's social geography on his first day, perfecting invisibility: sit center-left, answer second, never audition. A glimpse of the sealed east wing door unsettles him. Beat: the safety of being nobody, and its small cost.

chapters.title: The Ash Girl Assembly
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At orientation, the headmaster performs the school's founding myth, skipping neatly over the 1924 conservatory fire. Classmates joke about the Ash Girl ghost; Mirabel notices the drama teacher flinch. Beat: curiosity kindled against his will.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He finds a folded note in his locker: 'Mirabel. You hear it too, don't you?' The ink shimmers like cooled ash and won't smudge. No one else can see the writing. Beat: fear braided with a terrible thrill of being addressed.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with a scene from friend-skeptic Jun's POV. Mirabel tests the note—water, light, bleach—and it survives everything. Jun Park, his lab partner, catches him burning a corner and demands answers. Beat: the first crack in his isolation.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Forgot
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Jun's alternating POV. In the archive, a page of the 1924 yearbook is scorched to a single surviving name: Odile. The archivist, Ms. Verel, watches them too closely. Beat: the past is not missing—it was removed.

chapters.title: The Second Note
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Ash Girl leaves sheet music, half a melody, addressed to 'the one who hums in the stairwell'—something only Mirabel does. He realizes she has been watching him the way he watches everyone. Beat: seen, exposed, and strangely relieved.

chapters.title: Friends, Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Jun's POV. Jun swears Mirabel to secrecy and joins the hunt; popular Wren Sable catches them in the east wing and, instead of reporting them, admits she's heard humming too. Beat: an unlikely trio forms, and Mirabel's invisibility strategy collapses.

chapters.title: Audition Season
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Winter showcase sign-ups go live; the drama teacher, Mr. Calloway, pressures Mirabel to audition, saying he 'has the look of someone with something to say.' Mirabel refuses. That night, the note asks: 'Why do you hide your voice?' Beat: the theme of identity turns inward.

chapters.title: Odile's Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Wren's POV. Behind a false wall in the east wing they find a preserved practice room: a scorched violin, a diary with torn pages, a photograph of a girl with Mirabel's exact profile. Beat: the ghost's story becomes personal; dread arrives.

chapters.title: The Fairweather Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He calls his grandmother, who goes silent, then warns him: 'Some names we changed for good reason.' He learns his great-grandfather sat on the board that expelled Odile and sealed the fire's record. Beat: inheritance as guilt; loyalty to family vs. truth.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Jun's POV. The notes turn urgent—dates, deadlines, the words 'before the final audition.' Ms. Verel catches them in the archive and, instead of punishing them, reveals she has been waiting decades for someone to ask. Beat: an ally with her own buried reasons.

chapters.title: What Calloway Knows
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel spies on Mr. Calloway and finds him burning papers in the east wing—protecting the school's reputation, and something older. Confronted, Calloway warns that unsealing Odile's record will end scholarships, legacies, reputations. Beat: the cost of truth made concrete.

chapters.title: The Melody Completes Itself
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Ash Girl's notes now arrive as full music; playing it, Mirabel experiences her memory—expelled for a crime she didn't commit, locked in the conservatory the night it burned. Beat: empathy becomes testimony; he can no longer pretend neutrality.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a legacy student, faces her family's fury when she defends the investigation; Jun risks her scholarship. Mirabel, watching his friends pay prices he's avoided, realizes 'the new kid' was always a label he chose. Beat: loyalty tested; identity sharpened.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Ms. Verel produces the diary's missing pages, hidden for a century: proof the fire was set by a trustee—Mirabel's great-grandfather's closest friend—to destroy evidence of the expulsion. Beat: the full truth, and the full weight of it.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Corridor
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The school begins to change: ash-scented drafts, the east wing door found open, students dreaming the same burning melody. The administration blames 'senior pranks' and threatens expulsion for anyone involved. Beat: pressure peaks; the trio must commit or retreat.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The headmaster privately offers Mirabel a full scholarship and a clean record if he hands over the diary and lets it go. That night the Ash Girl's final note: 'You can stay invisible, or you can sing. Not both.' Beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Ghost
chapters.summary: Jun and Wren's POV. The trio prepares to expose the truth at the showcase: Wren will speak, Jun will project the records, and Mirabel—terrified, transformed—will perform Odile's completed piece. Beat: fear transmuted into purpose; the calm before the fire.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Onstage before the whole school, Mirabel plays the melody and tells Odile's story aloud as the east wing's sealed records ignite—harmlessly, theatrically—behind him, ash-inked pages raining proof. Beat: the climax; Mirabel is fully, publicly seen.

chapters.title: Her Name, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the smoke and silence, the Ash Girl appears one last time—no longer a rumor but a girl with a name, a face, a history restored to the record. She thanks him and lets go. Beat: grief and grace; memory honored, not haunted.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating trio POV. Fallout: the headmaster resigns, the conservatory's history enters the curriculum, Calloway quietly leaves. Mirabel's grandmother sends Odile's real violin with a letter of apology a century late. Beat: consequences, repair, and the ache of what was lost.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the spring showcase, Mirabel auditions under his own name, first in line, head up. Jun and Wren sit front row; a faint scent of ash and something sweeter drifts through the hall, approving. Beat: resolution—identity chosen, loyalty earned, memory kept alive.
